correctness.rationale: Both given graphs have six neighbors per vertex and two common neighbors per distinct pair, verified for all labels. This gives A²=4I+2J, with constant eigenvalue 6 and trace-determined multiplicities 6 and 9 for 2 and −2. Their root neighborhoods are respectively C6 and two disjoint triangles. A nonempty fort contained in the whites cannot lose its first vertex and a nonempty white closure is itself a fort. The independent 65,536-mask scan per graph computes simultaneous forcing by dynamic recursion to strictly smaller white masks. It reproduces the exact labeled coefficients and both minimum/total counts, comparing all 131,072 decisions against the two binary blocks by explicit bit order. Superset marking of newly found minimal forts in increasing order gives least obstruction sizes without a zeta transform; it agrees with the closure decision for every mask and gives minimal fort counts (60,48,336) and (60,144,112) at sizes 4,5,6 only, as well as both full five- and six-white classifications. A successful set is inclusion-minimal iff no one-vertex removal succeeds, by monotonicity; these scans give only size-ten minimal sets. The round counts at size ten are 1312/2304 for Shrikhande and 864/2592 for rook. For the symmetry check, the root has six neighbors forming a six-cycle; the other nine vertices have distinct two-neighbor signatures in it. Enumerating all images of the root and cycle permutations and checking the unique extensions gives exactly 192 automorphisms. The resulting 23 orbits match every CSV field, with sizes 192×15, 96×7 and 64 once. The two polynomials differ only at degrees ten and eleven by 160 and 96; the higher-degree equality has independently checked nonzero coefficients, not just a shared zero-forcing number.
residual_risks: These labeled counts and times concern ordinary forcing and the stated synchronous convention only. They do not assert a relation between spectra and polynomials for all strongly regular graphs.

evidence: The bipartite forest theorem covers every size of rook board: white-cell graph empty or an acyclic graph with an isolate on one side and a leaf on the other. At 4×4 the minimum formula gives 10 and 3456. The earlier fort polynomial counts all forts by cardinality; the later minimal-fort theorem classifies rook inclusion-minimal forts. Montazeri–Soltankhah's k=1 specialization gives the scalar mn−m−n+2.
broader_coverage.reasoning: These stronger rook-family results already determine the corresponding rook claims (not automatically the time counts). The Shrikhande graph is not a rook graph, as witnessed by the root neighborhood; no such specialization controls its ordinary counts or the pair comparison.

originality.rationale: The rook-side forcing polynomial and minimum sets are already covered by a stronger all-rook formula and are an expressly identified benchmark, not an originality credit. A later general classification also covers rook minimal forts. Abiad et al. give ordinary Z separation for a different cospectral pair, and for these exact two graphs give a PSD, not ordinary, separation. The supported distinct finding is that the standard full polynomials separate this canonical pair despite the equal standard minimum, with the Shrikhande counts, orbit/time data and exact comparative obstruction geometry. No checked statement or implication supplies that finding in full.
residual_risks: The 2024 Cartesian-product reference cited by the rook theorem was not recovered via the checked DOI route. That is not evidence of absence; the rook polynomial was independently identified as covered by the catalog theorem.
The audit does not establish historical priority, and an unindexed equivalent Shrikhande census or an alternative classification might exist.

value.rationale: A canonical pair of nonisomorphic strongly regular graphs with the same spectrum and the same ordinary forcing number is a natural controlled test of the extra information in the ordinary polynomial. The precise difference and fort-size thresholds make the distinction interpretable, and the Shrikhande orbit/time data make the exceptional minimum configurations usable as a benchmark. Independent value lies in the distinction and the Shrikhande side, not in rediscovering the rook polynomial.
residual_risks: The certified comparison is specific to these two graphs; it does not characterize the polynomial on cospectral graphs in general.
